text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Steel maker Hoogovens expects improvement in net result in 1997. (p1)
- Parliament demands Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm publishes report by stock market supervisors on collapse of Nusse Brink brokerage. (p1)
- Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers says retail franchises and independent affiliates free to continue setting up purchasing agreements. (p1)
- Food and beverages group BolsWessanen expects to make one or more big acquisitions this year. (p1)
- Food retail group Ahold books 1996 net up 38.5 pct at Dfl 632.4 million. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister rejects MPs' demands that new cartel authority should be allowed to check bank mergers. (p3)
- Automation company Cap Volmac VOLM.AS posts 1996 net up 25 pct at Dfl 90 million. (p4)
- Director of ailing M&S fashion unit to leave department store chain KBB (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Christian Democrat chairman fed up with former prime minister and party chiefs' criticism of party direction. (p1)
- Cable operators Casema and Castel reach agreement with PTT Telecom on interconnecting telephone traffic. (p2)
- Unions plead for more flexible pay and conditions agreements in banking sector. (p3)
- Philips Electronics concludes global spread of regional headquarters with new HQ in the U.S. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch banks return funds to relatives of Jewish victims of World War Two. (p1)
- Cheaper diesel for transport sector not feasible in the short term; parliament seeks alternatives. (p6)
- Confectioner Van Melle takes five percent stake in rival Klene. (p31)
- Pharmaceutical firm ACF declines profit forecast. (p31)
TROUW
- Dutch railways (NS) rival Lovers Rail seeks legal action over traffic minister's refusal to allow it to operate throughout Randstad region. (p3)
- Price agreement between PTT Telecom, Telfort and Enertel breaks EU competition rules, say other telecoms providers. (p7) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Fiscal stimulation for "green" investments proving very popular. (p1)
